commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix composition conditioned the Brazil IEEPA carve-out on the witness exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` rather than on Section 232 aluminum membership, so it charged the 40% Brazil surcharge on aluminum articles that headings 9903.01.83 / 9903.85.02 except from heading 9903.01.77.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 96 (read the diff in full): Brazil gate re-grounded in `ieepa_component_rate` (post line 2373) and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` (post line 2529); steel provenance re-cited on `ch99b_s232_steel_heading_rate` / `section_232_steel_component_rate` with the 0.50 rate, effective_from 2026-02-15 and the component formula unchanged. No other hunks. Same kind caveat (untraceable_branch vs wrong_entity_or_scope) and the same residual gap that the post-fix gate excepts only aluminum while 9903.01.83 also excepts iron/steel and other classes.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes an evaluated formula token in two rules (`ieepa_component_rate`, `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`), swapping the Brazil IEEPA carve-out gate from the witness's per-line exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` to the membership predicate `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`; the rules' own unchanged proof atom grounds that branch on "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02." Reading the provisions through the pinned release confirms the source: 9903.01.77 imposes the Brazil +40% "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90", and 9903.01.83 covers "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum ... of Brazil", so a chapter-wide composition gated on a single exemplar-line flag charged the surcharge on every other Brazil aluminum article the source excepts — a condition with no basis in the cited heading, re-grounded by the fix. I could not refute it as mechanical (a formula token, not a hash or string, changed) nor as new scope (the module claims schedule scale — its summary says it performs `chNN_general_rate[hts_line]` over the chapter table — and the flawed gate shipped on main in b2858d659 two days earlier, not just inside this PR stack). The second half of the diff (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02 on `ch99b_s232_steel_heading_rate`) is provenance-only and does not support the kind.

triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence trail: diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/198bee703e/098.diff; pre/post dumps at .../scratchpad/pre98.yaml and post98.yaml.

1) Only the Brazil gate carries the finding. The other half of the 58-line diff (`ch99b_s232_steel_heading_rate` and `section_232_steel_component_rate`) changes only the `source:` string and proof-atom `corpus_citation_path` from us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 + .88 to us/statute/hts/9903.82.02; the excerpt text, the parameter value `formula: '0.50'`, effective_from '2026-02-15', and the component formula are byte-identical pre/post. The resolver confirms 9903.81.87 does not resolve in this corpus vintage while 9903.82.02 exists at "+ 50%" — i.e. a stale-locator provenance correction, mechanical under the rubric. If a reviewer scopes the case to the steel parameter alone, it is mechanical, not fidelity.

2) The strongest refutation I tested and rejected: `entry_is_line_b` is also the formula of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded`, whose source line is "HTS 9903.01.33 section 232 metals article scope" — so one could argue the flag already *meant* "§232 metals article" and the swap is a rename. Against that: the PR body calls them "the witness's five per-line exemplar flags", the module summary distinguishes membership-semantic caller inputs from retained exemplar flags ("Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d because no membership module exists"), and the PR reports 18 explained non-equivalent witness cells, so the swap is not value-preserving.

3) Residual defect worth flagging to whoever consumes this corpus: post-fix, `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` STILL has `formula: entry_is_line_b` (post98.yaml line 1930) — the same exemplar-flag coupling survives in this module. And the fix is under-inclusive against the source: 9903.01.83 excepts Brazil iron/steel and derivatives, wood, vehicles and parts, semiconductors and copper as well as aluminum, so the post-fix encoding still charges the 40% on Brazil steel articles. Partial correction, but still a correction.

4) Kind runner-up: wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out covered one exemplar line rather than the §232 aluminum population). I kept untraceable_branch because the rubric explicitly covers a condition "with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it)", and the re-grounding is the essence of the change.

5) Caveat on module type: this is a generated `module.kind: composition` file, one of 100 near-identical chapter outputs of generator b1.6, so the underlying defect lives in the generator, and the same line appears in every sibling chapter module in this commit. It is still rulespec/v1 with rules and formulas, so I did not treat it as not_a_rule_module.
